summary: The root W-D-D primarily signifies love, affection, and desire. It encompasses wishing for something to happen or for someone to be in a certain state. It can also denote a strong, enduring fondness.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: وَدَّهُ, first pers. وَدِدْتُ, (S, M, L, Msb, K, &c.) and وَدَدْتُ, (Ks, Z, K,) [but most disallow this] aor. يَوَدُّ, inf. n. وُدٌّ and وِدٌّ and وَدٌّ, (S, M, L, K,) of which three forms the first is the most common, (MF,) and مَوَدَّةٌ, (S, M, L, K,) or this last is a simple subst., (Msb,) and مِوَدَّةٌ (CK and some MS. copies of the K) and مَوِدَّةٌ, (accord. to some other copies of the K, this and the next preceding deviating from the common forms of inf.
وادّهُ, inf. n. مُوَادَّةٌ and وِدَادٌ, He loved, or affected him, being loved, or affected, by him. (Msb.)
تودّدهُ He attracted to himself his love, or affection. (IAar, L, K.) تودّد إِلَيْهِ He manifested, or showed, love, or affection, to him. (L, Msb, K.)
هُمَا يَتَوَادَّانِ, (S, L,) inf. n. تَوَادٌّ, (K,) They two love, or affect, each other. (S, L, K.)

وِدٌّ (S, L, K) and (L, K) and (IJ, L, K) and (S, L, K) A person loved, or beloved; an object of love; a friend; syn. خِبٌّ and حَبِيبٌ and صَدِيقٌ (L) and مُحَبٌّ. (K: in the CK مُحِبٌّ.) Also, (TA) and (S, L, Msb) and (TA) and (Kz) A person who loves; loving; affectionate: (S, L, Msb, TA:) the first also used in a pl. sense, (L, K,) being [originally] an inf. n. (TA) and the second used alike as masc. and fem.

وَدٌّ: see 1, and وِدٌّ. وَدٌّ and (the former is the more common, L) A certain idol (S, L, K) which pertained to the people of Noah, and then to Kelb, and was at Doomet-el-Jendel: (S, L:) or a certain good man, who lived between Adam and Noah, and of whom, after his death, was made an image, which, after a long time, became an object of worship; like سُوَاعٌ and يَغُوثُ and يَعُوقُ and نَسْرٌ, mentioned therewith in the Kur, lxxi.

وُدٌّ: see 1, and وِدٌّ, and وَدٌّ. بِوُدِّى أَنْ يَكُونَ كَ َا I wish that such a thing may be. In the following saying of the poet, أَيُّهَا العَائِدُ المُسَائِلُ عَنَّا وَبِوُدِّيكَ لَوْ ثَرَى أَكْفَانِى [ O thou visitor of the sick, inquiring respecting us, wishing that thou mayest see my graveclothes ], the kesreh of the د is lengthened for sake of the measure. (S, L.)

وَدُودٌ: see وِدٌّ. الوَدُودُ, as an epithet applied to God, The loving towards his servants, (IAmb, L,) or, towards those who obey: (Beyd, lxxxv. 14:) or He who regards with approbation his righteous servants: or He who is beloved in the hearts of his saints. (IAth, L.)
أَوَدُّ More or most, loving or affectionate. Said to be also used as a pl., for أَوَدُّونَ. (L.)

مَوَدَّةٌ Love; affection. (Msb.) See also 1. Also, A letter; an epistle: and letters, or epistles: syn. كِتَابٌ and كُتُبٌ. (IAar, L, K.) Said to have the latter meaning in the Kur, lx. 1, in the first of the instances of its occurrence there: (L, K:) but this is a strange interpretation. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
